title: Consolidated rollout playbook with circuited shadow handoff
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a consolidated rollout playbook controller that coordinates canaries, A/B cohorts, and shadow handoffs with circuit breakers; includes new observability dashboards and documented runbooks.
description:
Motivation: Customers run complex model lifecycles (canaries, A/B tests, shadowing) and we have multiple small controllers and ad-hoc runbooks. This PR introduces a single, opinionated 'rollout playbook' controller that codifies common patterns (deferred shadow handoffs, cohort time-locks, circuited shadow drain) and provides safer automated rollback hooks.

Summary: Implement a controller + playbook DSL to: 1) stage canaries and AB cohorts, 2) mirror shadow traffic with an optional circuit-breaker that can pause/delay handoff when signal quality is low, 3) attach rollback policies to metric gates and smoke tests, 4) publish observability events for the Console and alerting. The change includes runtime behavior, e2e smoke tests, docs and a new Playbooks page in the docs site.

Design highlights: - Playbook DSL: small YAML schema supporting phases (shadow, canary, ramp, swap) and actions (pause, rollback, metric-gate). - Circuited shadow handoff: when shadow responses diverge beyond a configured similarity threshold or error rate, the circuit trips and the controller stalls handoff and notifies SRE/owner. The controller will optionally run a 'quarantine shadow' where a sampled subset of requests continue to mirror for offline replay. - Cohort time-lock: a minimum observation window per cohort to avoid noisy flips from transient signals. - Rollback policy hooks: policies tie to metric sets (latency, error, quality thresholds) and define immediate rollback, staged rollback or shadow quarantine. - Observability: new telemetry events (playbook.phase.enter, playbook.phase.exit, playbook.circuit.trip) and dashboards linked in the release notes.

Testing and validation: Unit coverage added for Playbook parsing and gate evaluation. Integration tests simulate a three-phase canary (shadow -> partial -> swap) with injected divergences; assertions verify that circuit trips and quarantine mode preserves traffic while blocking swap. An e2e smoke harness uses the benchmark-lab mock model to validate end-to-end telemetry.

Migration and operational notes: Existing ad-hoc rollout configs remain supported; the controller will only claim playbooks placed in 'rollouts/' CRD namespace. We document a migration path: convert existing YAML rules to the new playbook format using a provided script (scripts/convert-rollout-rules.py). The Console includes a preview page that renders the playbook timeline and current phase.

Risk and rollback: The controller adds opt-in behaviour, defaulting to a disabled state for accounts with active Dedicated/Private deployments until an admin enables it. Rollouts can be paused or instant-rolled back via the Console feature flags.

Related work: builds on ENG-3450 (rollout metrics gating) and reuses similarity scoring from ENG-4721.

Checklist: - [x] Playbook DSL parser and controller loop - [x] Circuit breaker and quarantine mode - [x] Unit + integration + e2e tests - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Console preview for playbooks

Commits: see commit_summary for a short list.

Merge method: squash and merge.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice consolidation. Question: how do we avoid duplication with the existing staged-rollout controller? Could this subsume it or should we keep both?

Maya Chen: The plan is to deprecate the smaller staged controller after a one-quarter migration window. This playbook is purposefully more opinionated and supports the legacy controller compatibility layer for a transition period.
Priya Nair: The circuit thresholds look reasonable but we should expose a 'probe-sensitivity' param for platform teams. Also add an audit log entry when a circuit trips.
Maya Chen: Added probeSensitivity and audit log emission; included notes in the runbook about tuning. See latest commits.
Liam O'Connor: Tests look solid. One nit: prefer explicit context timeouts in controller loops to avoid goroutine leaks.
Maya Chen: Addressed in controller_loop.go — timeouts added and tested.
notes_after_merge: Playbook controller will be rolled out to a small subset of hosted accounts over the next week. SRE will monitor playbook.circuit.trip metrics and page on sustained trips. Migration script available at scripts/convert-rollout-rules.py.
